items.title: The right equipment for a genuinely heavy, awkward item
text: Pianos move on piano boards, dollies and moving straps designed for their exact weight distribution — not a furniture dolly and good intentions. items.title: Donation-first for pianos that still play
text: A piano that still works deserves a second home before it becomes junk. Live Junk Free checks with donation partners — schools, community centres, churches and music programs — before defaulting to recycling, so a functioning upright or grand often finds its way to someone who’ll actually play it.

items.title: Responsible piano recycling for pianos that don't
text: Pianos that are damaged, water-warped or simply beyond playing get broken down for proper piano recycling: the cast iron plate and metal strings go to metal recyclers, the wooden cabinet is disposed of responsibly, and keys or components containing older materials are handled appropriately rather than just landfilled.

blocks.text: PIANO REMOVAL FAQ
Piano Removal in Toronto — What to Know Before You Book

items.q: How much does piano removal cost in Toronto?
a: Pricing is confirmed on site once the crew sees the piano’s type, size and the path out — an upright or console costs less than a full grand piano, and stairs or tight access never add a surcharge. The piano removal cost covers the move, any needed disassembly and the disposal or recycling together, and it’s the same number whether you searched “piano removal cost” or “piano haul away cost” to find us.

items.q: Do you charge extra for stairs?
a: No. Narrow staircases, turning stairwells and multi-floor moves are factored into one flat quote at the walkthrough, not billed as an add-on. A piano on the third floor of a Toronto walk-up prices the same formula as one on the ground floor — the crew and equipment adjust, not the honesty of the number.

items.q: Can you remove a piano from a condo or apartment building?
a: Yes, and it’s handled by the building’s book. Certificates of insurance go to management at booking, freight elevators reserve ahead, and hallways and common areas get protected throughout the move.

items.q: What's involved in moving a grand or baby grand piano?
a: More disassembly than most people expect. Legs, the lid and sometimes the pedal lyre come off to fit through doorways and stairwells, the piano moves on proper piano boards, and everything reassembles correctly at the destination if it’s going to a donation recipient rather than being recycled.

items.q: Do you offer piano pick up the same day I call?
a: Often, yes. Trucks run Toronto daily, 6AM to 11PM, seven days a week, so a morning call frequently means a same-day piano pickup — call +1 647 922 5865 for today’s real availability.

items.q: What happens to the piano once it's removed — is it just junk piano removal?
a: Not by default. We check with donation partners — schools, community centres, churches and music programs — before anything is recycled, so a piano that still plays often gets a second life. Only pianos that are genuinely beyond use go to piano recycling, where the metal frame and strings are separated for metal recyclers and the wood cabinet disposed of responsibly.

items.q: Is there a difference between piano removal and general junk removal?
a: Yes, meaningfully. Junk removal piano jobs handled by a general hauler often lack the specific equipment and technique pianos require — the wrong dolly, no leg-removal experience, no donation checks first. Piano removal is a specialized service, and Live Junk Free’s crews are experienced specifically with the weight distribution, disassembly and care involved.

items.q: Can you remove a piano from a house we're settling as part of an estate?
a: Regularly, and gently. The piano and anything else in the room or home clear at the family’s pace, with donation coordination offered first given how often a piano carries sentimental as well as musical value, and documentation available if the estate needs it.
